title: A to Z
rule: Twenty-six small captions in order, the first word of each beginning with the next letter of the alphabet.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
made: storyboard sheet of seven boards (six half-width, the last full width) on the LoC 1934 sheet, each with a graphite header naming its letters ('board 3   F - H')

the page-03 engraving puppets reused: AGENT = the 1863 telegraph operator cut into pinned limbs (brass pins), STRANGER = the 1867 Steinway Hall woman; the engraved window and table from the same plates
set in the shared pen hand (HANDMADE): clock (4:08 / 4:10 / 4:11), memo, cupboard hinged on the left jamb with the key on its hook and SERVICE tag, SERVICE door
26 pasted torn slips pinned with brass pins, one caption each, each opening on a larger red pen initial; the captions run A to Z in board order
captions: At Randolph, the agent at his desk.
Before him, a memo:
Clear enough: '4:15 - open SERVICE door. Key in cupboard.'
Dutifully he rises.
Errand in mind, he sets off across the office.
From the window, a voice.
Gloved, hatted, a stranger leans in.
Her words: 'Pardon me — have you the right time?'
In reply he turns to the clock.
Just ten past four.
Kindly he answers: 'Ten past four, by the clock.'
Lightly she nods.
'Much obliged!' she says.
Now the window is empty.
On he goes to the cupboard.
Pulling the door, he opens it.
Quite plainly:
Right on its hook, the key, tagged SERVICE.
Silence.
The pencil drifts to his chin.
Unable to think why he came, he asks himself:
Very quietly: 'Well, here I am... and what for?'
Words fail him.
X marks the spot: the key still hangs there.
Yet he never takes it.
Zero errands done: the SERVICE door stays closed.

events.E1: board 3 (F-H) the window; H quotes the question
events.E2: board 4 (I-K) clock at 4:10; K quotes the answer
events.E3: board 5 (L-N) she nods and goes; M quotes the thanks
events.E4: board 6 (O-R) the cupboard opened, the key on its hook tagged SERVICE
events.E5: board 7 (S-Z) pencil to chin; V quotes the forgetting line; X/Y/Z: the key still hangs, he never takes it, the SERVICE door stays closed

substitutions: none: the four lines verbatim, quoted inside captions H, K, M (opening quote mark before its M) and V
beat: the boards fill with their slips one board at a time, the red initials marching A to Z

self_check.check: The caption initials run A to Z (measured: first letter of each of the 26 captions asserted ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ at build time; caption M begins with an opening quote mark before 'Much')
self_check.evidence: measured (initials, size, bytes) and perceptually judged (from frames) by the maker

weaknesses: X is the usual cheat ('X marks the spot')
the puppets and the window plate repeat page 03's material closely; boards 3-5 share one composition
the engraved puppets are dark and busy at the small board scale; the slips carry most of the story
